rule: Each row is a bounded candidate for a separate successor validation. This protocol changes no matrix cell, terminal state, class state, publication state, or graph.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Montana’s captured operative authority is the approved FFY 2026 original SNAP E&T state plan.
rows.evidence_basis: The document identifies Montana, federal fiscal year 2026, Original Submission, and an approved form status.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This establishes the captured plan identity and version only; it does not establish uniform frontline practice.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: The captured implementation authority is temporally bounded to the FFY 2026 state plan, approved September 11, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The plan is designated FFY 2026 and records approval on September 11, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: Approval and plan-year identity do not establish the effective date of every subordinate policy.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Montana’s captured screening surface uses eligibility staff plus CHIMES business rules at application/interview, with signed application and recertification forms serving as work-registration verification.
rows.evidence_basis: The plan describes screening by eligibility staff and CHIMES using application and interview data, and identifies signed application/recertification forms as work-registration verification.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This establishes the stated screening process, not uniform execution or a person-level decision.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Nebraska’s captured verification surface permits multiple evidence classes rather than one mandatory document type.
rows.evidence_basis: The flyer states documentary evidence is primary but not exclusive and permits household documents, electronic data, collateral contacts, other agencies or organizations, and other reliable sources.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is a general verification rule; it does not prove how discretion was exercised in any case.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: North Dakota’s captured operative authority is the approved FFY 2026 original SNAP E&T state plan.
rows.evidence_basis: The document identifies North Dakota, FFY 2026, Original Submission, and an approved form status.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This establishes the captured plan identity/version only.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: The captured implementation authority is temporally bounded to the FFY 2026 plan approved September 29, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The plan is designated FFY 2026 and records approval on September 29, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The plan-year and approval date do not establish every subordinate policy effective date.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: North Dakota’s captured screening surface is an eligibility-worker interactive interview at application, review, and relevant changes, with ABAWD-exception screening.
rows.evidence_basis: The plan describes an eligibility-worker interactive interview at application, review, and relevant reported changes, including work-requirement exemptions and ABAWD exceptions.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This establishes the stated screening process, not uniform frontline practice.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: South Dakota’s captured operative authority is the SNAP Policy and Procedure Manual updated July 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The document identifies itself as the South Dakota SNAP Policy and Procedure Manual updated July 2026.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The captured title/update establishes document identity and recency, not that every provision became effective in July 2026.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: South Dakota’s captured rule states that evident physical or mental impairment needs no further verification; otherwise specified disability evidence may be used.
rows.evidence_basis: The manual contains dedicated work-registration and ABAWD chapters and states how apparent or non-apparent physical or mental impairment is verified.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is the written rule and verification surface, not proof of uniform administration.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: South Dakota’s captured verification surface permits documentary evidence and collateral contacts, with case-record narration and specialist judgment.
rows.evidence_basis: The manual permits collateral contacts where documentary evidence is not readily available and assigns Benefits Specialist documentation responsibilities.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish a person-level outcome or uniform exercise of discretion.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: West Virginia’s captured current ABAWD clock is January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2027.
rows.evidence_basis: The notice states the current 36-month period begins January 1, 2025 and ends December 31, 2027.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The clock is not by itself a geographic-waiver approval or statewide waiver disposition.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: West Virginia’s captured fitness rule recognizes medically certified physical or mental unfitness for employment.
rows.evidence_basis: The notice lists medically certified physical or mental unfitness as an ABAWD exemption.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish how certification is assessed in a particular case.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Arkansas’s captured ABAWD time-limit implementation date is July 1, 2023.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states that the time-limit rules resumed on July 1, 2023.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the rule page and does not establish later amendments not shown there.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Arkansas’s captured fitness/work-rule surface applies to the stated age and household group when considered physically and mentally able to work, with an 80-hour monthly threshold.
rows.evidence_basis: The page applies the rule to recipients considered physically and mentally able to work and states the 80-hour monthly threshold.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not prove uniform staff determinations.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: California’s captured implementation date for the stated work and community-engagement changes is June 1, 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states changed California rules apply as of June 1, 2026.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the page’s described change set.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: California’s captured waiver covers Alpine, Colusa, Imperial, Merced, Monterey, Plumas, and Tulare Counties from November 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The page identifies seven counties waived from November 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish waiver status outside those counties or after the stated end date.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: California’s captured fitness rule uses ability to work at least 20 hours weekly and recognizes inability due to physical or mental health.
rows.evidence_basis: The page defines the ABAWD group as physically and mentally able to work at least 20 hours weekly and lists physical/mental-health inability as an excuse.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not prove a person-level classification.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Florida’s captured fitness rule recognizes medically certified physical or mental unfitness, with DCF determination.
rows.evidence_basis: The page lists medically certified physical or mental unfitness and says DCF makes the determination when a person reports inability to meet work requirements.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is the stated rule, not proof of uniform adjudication.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Georgia’s captured implementation date for the described expanded ABAWD requirements is November 1, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states Georgia implementation for the described expanded requirements begins November 1, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the described change set.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Georgia’s captured screening surface applies the ABAWD rule to physically and mentally fit individuals and uses caseworker screening/interview.
rows.evidence_basis: The page describes fit-for-work criteria and caseworker interview/screening.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish uniform frontline application.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Maryland’s captured implementation date for the described expanded ABAWD requirements is November 1, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states expanded requirements begin November 1, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the described change set.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Maryland’s captured fitness rule recognizes physical or mental inability to work.
rows.evidence_basis: The page recognizes physical or mental inability to work as an exemption.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The source does not establish a person-level determination.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Missouri’s captured verification surface permits multiple document types and submission channels.
rows.evidence_basis: The page lists multiple submission channels and verification documents, including doctor and VA records.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This establishes available verification mechanics, not a person-level outcome.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Nevada’s captured verification surface includes worker assistance and collateral-contact verification.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states the worker may help obtain verification and permits collateral contacts.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish uniform exercise of discretion.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: North Carolina’s captured implementation date for the described revised requirements is December 1, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states revised work requirements take effect December 1, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the described change set.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: North Carolina’s captured screening rule allows no documentation when inability is obvious; otherwise a medical statement may be required, with caseworker assistance and a proof period.
rows.evidence_basis: The page describes caseworker screening, at least ten days to provide proof, obvious-condition treatment, and medical-statement verification.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is the written rule and process, not proof of uniform administration.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Oregon’s captured fitness rule recognizes inability to work because of physical, mental, or behavioral health.
rows.evidence_basis: The page recognizes physical, mental, or behavioral-health inability as an exemption.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish a person-level determination.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Pennsylvania’s captured implementation surface identifies staged changes beginning September 1 and November 1, 2025.
rows.evidence_basis: The page identifies staged rule changes beginning September 1 and November 1, 2025.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the described change set.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Pennsylvania’s captured current waiver disposition is that no county or municipality qualifies for an ABAWD geographic waiver.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states Pennsylvania no longer qualifies for county or municipal waivers.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is a current page statement and does not establish future waiver status.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Pennsylvania’s captured fitness rule recognizes physical or mental inability to work.
rows.evidence_basis: The page recognizes physical or mental inability to work.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish a person-level determination.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Rhode Island’s captured implementation boundary is a new ABAWD clock beginning September 1, 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states a new 36-month clock begins September 1, 2026.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not independently supply an end date for that clock.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Rhode Island’s captured fitness surface provides DHS routing to identify a recipient as unfit for work and an exemption form with documentation requirements.
rows.evidence_basis: The page describes able-to-work status and DHS routing for an unfit-for-work determination.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish a person-level determination or spell out a complete medical standard.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Washington’s captured implementation date for the stated time-limit rules is February 1, 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states the time-limit rules are effective February 1, 2026 for the described group.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This is bounded to the page’s stated rule.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Washington’s captured current geographic-waiver disposition is no exempt area as of February 1, 2026.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states no areas are exempt as of February 1, 2026.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish future waiver status.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Washington’s captured fitness rule recognizes physical or mental inability to work.
rows.evidence_basis: The page recognizes physical or mental inability to work as an exemption.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish a person-level determination.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Washington’s captured verification surface gives the household choice among acceptable proof types and assigns agency assistance/cost responsibility.
rows.evidence_basis: The page states applicants may choose the type of verification and the agency can help obtain or pay for proof.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: This does not establish a person-level result.

rows.candidate_bounded_finding: Wisconsin’s captured basic-work-rule surface recognizes physical or mental inability to work, subject to agency determination.
rows.evidence_basis: The page recognizes physical or mental inability and describes agency determination.
rows.counterevidence_or_limitation: The page does not establish a person-level determination.
